P1.evidence: P1a is a clear miss rather than not applicable: an application exists and the prospect pointedly referenced it in his first sentence — 'Well, I was pretty descriptive with the... Filling out everything, but really, man' — and again later, 'like I filled out when the questionnaire'. Nothing was read back. The usual two-part frame ran ('where are you today? Where do you want to be? If we can help, I can show you one of the many options') with a thin 'Okay? Yep' for agreement. Open question ran cleanly.

P2.evidence: Not a single baseline question was asked. Age (36) and body fat (around 8%) were volunteered; height and weight were never established. Work was covered in substance across the call but never asked as a baseline item and the desk-bound question never ran. The injury was volunteered in the opening answer and the rep engaged with it repeatedly, which earns a partial on P2d — but he never asked the questions that matter here: what are you cleared to do, when does clearance come, and who is managing it. The prospect volunteered the answer anyway ('I'm not cleared to do like a lot of lifting') and it changed nothing. Training week, current results, diet, sleep and energy were all skipped; the extensive nutrition detail came unprompted from the prospect and later his wife.

P3.evidence: The best single question in the batch opened this phase: 'are you looking to get back into shape or are you looking to be your best?' — which reframed the whole call and got 'To be my best.' Followed with 'Why is that important for you?', then the empty-cup bridge, 'by your cup being full, maybe even overflown, how do you foresee that pouring into your community?', and 'Where do you want to be at 40?' That sequence produced leadership, marriage, future children, legacy, service and charitable giving. Only the explicit reflect-back was never delivered.

P4.evidence: Skipped almost entirely. No 'what have you tried', no 'what happened with that', no 'why didn't it stick', and — unusually for this rep, who runs it on most calls — no P4f at all: he never asked why coaching rather than doing it himself. The prospect supplied the gap unprompted and precisely ('a struggle of mine has been consistency because it kind of comes easy for me' and 'I need structure. I need a team that I can plug into or accountability. So I know that that's a missing link'), which earns partials, but the script credits asking and nothing was asked.

P5.evidence: P5a ran with a well-judged softener — 'God isn't going to come down and strike thunder in your house if you don't lift a few kettlebells. But I'm curious, what does the future look like for yourself if you don't go up that gear?' The want-or-need question stood in for the settle check and got 'I feel like it's a need, for sure' with a real reason attached (still capable at 46 and 56, running around with kids and grandkids). No 'why not' and no proper line in the sand — 'Time, time for action, as they say' is not the move.

P6.evidence: The 1-10 check ran and, unusually, got an honest sub-10 answer — 'I would say an eight, seven to eight. I'm not going to say 10, just because I feel like that would be kind of naive' — and the rep followed it properly with 'what gives you the confidence to say that we can potentially help you?' P6b never ran, which is the third call in this batch where its absence let a spouse-plus-finances blocker appear only after the price. He did eventually run the equivalent isolate — 'putting the investment aside for a moment, do you want to do this?' / '100% I do' — but twenty minutes downstream of where the script wants it.

P11.evidence: The only complete Phase 11 in this batch. Payment collected and confirmed live through Paver after Klarna declined ('Congrats, your approval' / 'I've just seen it, man. You're in'). Trevor onboarding call offered as specific slots and booked for Wednesday 4:15pm Central. Agreement email confirmed as arrived and e-signed on the call — 'Take your time, look at it, sign it' / 'I'll go through this and then I just need to e-sign it.' P11d is partial: app and Skool access were explained and the rep walked him through joining the community, but the onboarding questionnaire was never mentioned and the Skool invite had not landed by the end of the call.

objection_plays.detail: The most complete money play in the batch. Isolated cleanly ('putting the investment aside for a moment, do you want to do this?' — '100% I do'), ran the upfront-versus-instalments line ('Most people put it on the credit card. But we have in-house payment plan options, if necessary'), and got a genuine financial picture: monthly surplus asked directly ('how much per month would not implicate things too much for you guys?' — $250), break-even ($7,800/month), existing obligations (truck and elbow at roughly $700/month), credit score (758, asked outright) and future income ($31,000 contract). NOT run: number of credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, investments, and the 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' frame. The material criticism is not the play but the use of it — having established a $250/month ceiling, he closed at $650/month against a future payment rather than building to the stated capacity.

Played through to the best available outcome. Got her name, confirmed she knew about the call, asked what could prevent them moving forward, and ran the permission-versus-FYI question near-verbatim: 'when you speak to Gabrielle, is that a, like a, when I say this with respect, like a permission thing, or is it just like an FYI kind of thing?' The prospect then brought her onto the call live, she asked her own substantive questions and approved. NOT run: 'Is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain?' and 'This isn't a joint decision like buying a house.' Skipping those was the right call — bringing her in beat working around her.

Triggered explicitly — 'it's not all that great of a time frame... I just feel like it's something in that regard that I should probably wait.' None of the scripted moves ran: no 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets'. The rep improvised instead, and effectively, off the prospect's own disclosure: 'if we know that we're getting that significant chunk of change in one go... Why not get started in this moment, knowing that you're going to make that money next month?' plus a downside cover ('we're not animals... we can pause the program for you'). Better suited to the prospect than the script would have been, but scored as partial because the play itself did not run.

The clinical gap, and this is the clearest instance in the corpus. The prospect volunteered in his opening answer that he is not medically cleared to lift and has two to three weeks to go. There is no scripted gate requiring the rep to stop, verify clearance, or defer the start date, so the disclosure passed through the entire call without consequence and he was booked into a live movement session before his clearance date. Separately, his wife asked directly whether anyone on staff has rehabilitation expertise and the script has no answer for that either. Both are process defects, not rep failures.

notes: Process-wise the strongest call in the batch: the 'back into shape or be your best' reframe, a real financial-picture conversation, a spouse brought onto the call and satisfied rather than managed, and the only Phase 11 executed end to end. It is also the call with the most serious unaddressed clinical disclosure, and the two facts are independent — a well-run call sold a not-yet-cleared post-surgical prospect a loaded programme and booked him into a movement assessment before his clearance date. Phases 2 and 4 were skipped wholesale; everything the rep knew about this man's body, diet and history, the man volunteered himself.
